Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 06.11.2023 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bidar, in MVC No.365 of 2022.

sentences.text: 3. The claimant, aged 34 years met with an accident on 14.06.2021 and sustained grievous injures.

Therefore, she filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.13,25,000/-
with interest at 12% p.a.
She stated that she was earning Rs.15,000/- per NC: 2025:KHC-K:6766 HC-KAR month.

The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record, awarded a global compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, she sustained fracture of left nasal bone and fracture of right clavicle; she was an inpatient for ten days as per the claim petition; she has difficulty in attending her domestic work and thus, requested for enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6. The appellant has produced Ex.P3-wound certificate.
As per the wound certificate, she has sustained three fractures.

She has not produced any record to show that she was hospitalised for ten Raisa Begum vs Khadeer Pasha And Anr on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66347972/
2 days.

sentences.text: Except her statement, there is no other record before this Court.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6766 HC-KAR Except filing FIR, complaint and wound certificate, the appellant has not filed any other documents and she has not even examined the Doctor.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that, assessment of loss of future earnings would not arise.

However, considering the nature of injuries, it is reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- for injuries, Rs.10,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- for loss of amenities, Rs.10,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges and Rs.5,000/- for medical expenses.
7. Further, the appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of two months due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
She has not filed any income proof.
Therefore, as the accident is of the year 2021, her income is to be taken as Rs.14,250/- as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Thus, she is entitled for an amount of Rs.28,500/-
towards loss of income during laid up period.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6766 HC-KAR 8.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Injuries Rs.30,000/-
Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.5,000/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.10,000/-
and attendant charges

Loss of income during laid up period Rs.28,500/-
Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.93,500/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.50,000/-
Enhancement Rs.43,500/-
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.43,500/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

9. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.43,500/- with interest at NC: 2025:KHC-K:6766 HC-KAR 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
